hypothesis: Injecting the 2 most similar gold exemplars as few-shot demonstrations should help the 3B model produce less redundant, more decision-critical questions, because seeing worked examples of high-quality question sets at inference time gives the model a concrete pattern to follow.
technique: At runtime, 2 nearest non-dev gold exemplars are retrieved from a hard-coded pool of 12 via word-overlap Jaccard similarity, then injected as few-shot demonstrations into the system prompt, followed by a single greedy FM call to generate the final questions.
result: Scored 0.320 on dev-10 (0 wins / 1 tie / 9 losses vs Sonnet), a +0.013 gain over the baseline and a new best. Non-redundancy improved from 3 to 4, and the experiment produced the first tie vs gold, but coverage stayed at 3 with critical gaps (budget, departure city, group size) and the model still made catastrophic errors — confirming RAG scaffolding helps non-redundancy but cannot reliably surface decision-critical unknowns.
